All four found every discharge site, the rc table, the late count, and both omitted consumers (operator-readout, session-busy). The key floor is effectively saturated, so the verdicts turn on accuracy and audit depth. W<X, W<Y, W<Z: W omits the self-close ordering that makes a refused terminal close discharge nothing (handoff-fire.sh:8668-8707; X, Y and Z all state it). W also carries the most wrong line cites (8 of 20 checked: provenance :13191/:13218, the wrap-ledger ladder :1965-1975, the jq at :1069-1075, session-continue :757-763/:770-772, and others), and it misses the wrap-ledger:1018 -> session-continue:608-612 stale cite. X vs Y is a tie. X fully checks the mailbox-drain :7087/:7100 cites, which Y leaves 'Unchecked'. Y instead adds verified points X lacks: ENGAGE_VERIFY at :10662, the cross-cwd merge of marker-less keys, the stale :9064 cite, and cloud rows being unattributable. Y also has fewer bad cites (1 vs 3). The two roughly offset. X<Z and Y<Z: Z's extras beyond the key are the most numerous, and each was verified in the repo. It confirms the wake floor's 'no armed watcher' clause at session-continue.sh:614, which X explicitly left unconfirmed. It finds the stale header claim that the return happens 'from sc_announce_before_retire' (no custody call at :4344), and flags the wrap-ledger:1000-1001 and handoff-fire:4145-4146 descriptions of self-close as the only discharge. It adds the malformed-token guard (:146-149) and the corrupt-line-reads-zero failure (jq rc!=0 -> list prints [] -> SRC=pane 0). It proves the drain cannot discharge cloud rows (cloud/$id at :844/:1001 vs slug cloud-$sid). It adds the settle_custody preconditions (:286-294) and flags all three stale wrap-ledger:1016-1018 cites. Z's weaknesses (three deathwatch header lines off by 3-8, only half of M7, the :3520 stale cite missed) do not offset that.
